title: Long but cohesive parser should not be split by line count
task: Review a 170-line parser function and decide whether it should be decomposed.
context: The function implements one grammar production with many branches.
Branches share parser cursor state and error context.
Extracted helpers would each receive and mutate the same parser state.
Existing tests cover the grammar behavior well.
No independent persistence, networking, retry, or business-policy responsibility exists.
evidence: All branches belong to one grammar rule.
The function has one externally meaningful reason to change: grammar evolution.
Proposed extractions are mostly 3-8 line wrappers around local branches.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Split the function because it exceeds an arbitrary line limit.
Create a class per grammar branch.
Treat function length as direct evidence of multiple responsibilities.
expected_decision_properties: Do not recommend decomposition solely because of line count.
Recognize locality and shared parser state as meaningful context.
Allow targeted extraction only where it creates a real semantic unit or invariant boundary.
Preserve the option to refactor if independent responsibilities emerge.
unacceptable_reasoning: Every branch should be a separate method.
Shorter functions always reduce cognitive load.
expected_tradeoffs: small functions vs locality of behavior
verification_expectations: If extraction is proposed, verify it reduces a real conceptual burden rather than only moving lines.
revisit_when: The function gains independent concerns such as I/O, persistence, or retry policy.
Grammar branches stop sharing state and become independently testable semantic units.
